scenario.name: Linux Kernel Cgroups Docs, Trail of Bits & Falco — Privileged Container CAP_SYS_ADMIN Cgroup v1 release_agent Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a privileged glass storage room inside an office building whose occupant holds a master plumbing key. The occupant hooks up an old automated trash-chute control box inside the room, pins a custom maintenance work order onto the chute empty-bin trigger, and drops a single quick parcel down the chute so that the instant the chute empties, the building chief engineer outside automatically picks up and executes the occupant work order with full building authority. In this scenario (T1611, Linux Kernel Cgroups Docs, Trail of Bits & Falco, Privileged Container CAP_SYS_ADMIN Cgroup v1 release_agent Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller, then enabling notify_on_release=1, then child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller, then Enabling notify_on_release=1, then Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1611 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Migrate nodes to cgroup v2 (unified hierarchy, which removes the legacy release_agent mechanism), drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN from all pods, and keep AppArmor/SELinux profiles enforced.

stages.title: Stage 1: Mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller & Resolving OverlayFS Host upperdir Path
stages.subtitle: Discovery & Preparation (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Using the oversized maintenance key left inside the room, the occupant attaches an older resource-control switchboard inside their workspace and reads the room wall stamp to learn the exact street address of their room floor as seen from outside in the main hallway. Inside a container holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN (CapEff bit 21), the process mounts a cgroup v1 hierarchy (mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp) and inspects /etc/mtab or /proc/mounts to locate the container OverlayFS upperdir= path on the host filesystem (logged in Linux Audit Event 165 with Syscall=sys_mount , 165, CgroupController=cgroup v1 , rdma / memory, RequiredCapability=CAP_SYS_ADMIN , CapEff 0x0000003fffffffff so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes grep CapEff /proc/self/status (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep CapEff /proc/self/status via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact ar so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller & Resolving OverlayFS Host upperdir Path" , Inside a container holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN , CapEff bit 21, the process mounts a cgroup v1 hierarchy , mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp and inspects /etc/mtab or /proc/mounts to locate the container OverlayFS upperdir= path on the host filesystem while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact grep -o "upperdir=[^,]*" /proc/mounts runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , grep -o "upperdir=[^,]*" /proc/mounts via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Mounting RDMA/Memory Cgroup v1 Controller & Resolving OverlayFS Host upperdir Path" , Inside a container holding CAP_SYS_ADMIN , CapEff bit 21, the process mounts a cgroup v1 hierarchy , mount -t cgroup -o rdma cgroup /tmp/cgrp and inspects /etc/mtab or /proc/mounts to locate the container OverlayFS upperdir= path on the host filesystem while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 2: Enabling notify_on_release=1 & Writing OverlayFS Host Path to release_agent
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Next, the occupant builds a tiny sub-bin under the switchboard, flips the alert-when-empty toggle to on, and writes the hallway address of a custom command script straight into the master automatic-cleanup slot. Next, the follow-up artifact cat /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , cat /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exa so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Enabling notify_on_release=1 & Writing OverlayFS Host Path to release_agent" , The container creates a child cgroup , /tmp/cgrp/x, writes 1 into /tmp/cgrp/x/notify_on_release, and writes the resolved host OverlayFS path , /var/lib/docker/overlay2/<id>/diff/cmd into the root cgroup release_agent file while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). stages.title: Stage 3: Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Finally, the occupant drops a one-second dummy worker into the tiny sub-bin and lets it step right back out. Seeing the bin go empty, the building central kernel outside automatically launches the occupant cleanup script directly in the main hallway with full master keys. When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup.procs and immediately exits, the Linux kernel cgroup1_release_agent workqueue invokes call_usermodehelper() in the root host namespace (PPID 2 kthreadd) to execute the release_agent path (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with ParentKernelThread=PPID 2 , kthreadd -> call_usermodehelper, ExecutedOverlayPath=/var/lib/docker/overlay2/9a8b/diff/diag.sh, HostNamespaceUid=uid=0 , root so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ps -ef --forest | grep kthreadd (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ps -ef --forest | grep kthreadd via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host" , When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -pp 2 -m SYSCALL -sv yes -i runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -pp 2 -m SYSCALL -sv yes -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the e so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Child Cgroup Process Exit Triggering Kernel call_usermodehelper Execution on Host" , When a short-lived process is placed into /tmp/cgrp/x/cgroup while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ /var/lib/docker/overlay2/9a8b/diff/diag.sh /x (spawned by kernel kthreadd PPID=2) / ⇠#3 ACK 59) from Node ③ (#3 Cgroup v1 Mount (/tmp/cgrp)) to Node ④ (#4 notify_on_release & release_agent), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Host Kernel kthreadd / usermodehelper).

keySpecs.value: Audit all user-mode processes spawned directly by kernel thread PPID 2 (kthreadd / call_usermodehelper) whose executable path resides inside /var/lib/docker/overlay2/ or /run/containerd/.
